[2022 summer phd math-stat — problem 2]

Training data $(x_i, y_i)$, $1 \le i \le n$, are i.i.d. as $(x, y)$ with $y = x^T \beta^* + \varepsilon$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^p$, $\varepsilon$ independent of $x$, under (A1) $\varepsilon$ sub-Gaussian with parameter $\sigma$: $P(|\varepsilon| \ge t) \le 2e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}$; (A2) $|x| \le B_0$ a.s. Let $\hat\beta = \arg\min_\beta \{\ell_n(\beta) + \lambda\|\beta\|_1\}$ with $\ell_n(\beta) = \frac{1}{2n}\sum_i (y_i - x_i^T\beta)^2$. Let $(x_0, y_0)$ be an independent test point; study the out-of-sample error $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}$ (conditional on training data). Set $\lambda_0 = \sqrt{\log(p/\delta)/n}$. You may use results from preceding questions regardless of whether you answered them.
(i) Show $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\} = \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\beta^*)^2\} + \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(x_0^T(\hat\beta - \beta^*))^2\}$.
(ii) With $\Sigma = \mathbb{E}(x x^T)$ and $\tilde\Sigma = n^{-1}\sum_i x_i x_i^T$: for sufficiently small $\delta > 0$, show with probability $1 - k_1\delta$ that $\|\tilde\Sigma - \Sigma\|_{\max} \le B_1\lambda_0$ (constant $B_1$ depending on $B_0$). Call this event $\Omega_1$.
(iii) Under (A3) $b^T\Sigma b \ge (\nu_0^*)^2 \sum_j b_j^2$ and (A4) $|S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0 \le \eta_0$: show that on $\Omega_1$, $\nu_0^2(\sum_{j \in S_{\beta^*}}|b_j|)^2 \le |S_{\beta^*}|(b^T\tilde\Sigma b)$ for any $b$ with $\sum_{j \notin S_{\beta^*}}|b_j| \le \xi_0 \sum_{j \in S_{\beta^*}}|b_j|$ (a restricted-eigenvalue / compatibility condition on $\tilde\Sigma$).
(iv) Under (A1)-(A4), formulate an event $\Omega_2$ with $P(\Omega_2) \ge 1 - k_2\delta$ such that on $\Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2$, for a suitable $\lambda$: $\frac1n\sum_i (x_i^T(\hat\beta - \beta^*))^2 \le M_0 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2$ and $\|\hat\beta - \beta^*\|_1 \le M_0 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0$. Prove $P(\Omega_2) \ge 1 - k_2\delta$ for your $\Omega_2$ (you need not prove the two displayed bounds).
(v) For that $\lambda$, show on $\Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2$ that $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\} \le \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\beta^*)^2\} + M_1 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2$.

Let  
\[
S=S_{\beta^*}:=\{j:\beta_j^*\neq 0\},\qquad s=|S|,
\]
and write  
\[
h:=\hat\beta-\beta^*,\qquad 
\|v\|_n^2:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i^Tv)^2=v^T\widetilde\Sigma v.
\]

I will use the standard convention in this linear model that  
\[
\mathbb E(\varepsilon)=0,
\]
which is necessary for part (i). If \(\mathbb E\varepsilon\neq 0\), an additional cross term appears.

---

## (i) Bias–variance/excess-risk decomposition

Condition on the training data, so \(\hat\beta\) and hence \(h=\hat\beta-\beta^*\) are fixed. For an independent test point,
\[
y_0=x_0^T\beta^*+\varepsilon_0.
\]
Thus
\[
y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta
=\varepsilon_0-x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)
=\varepsilon_0-x_0^Th.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
&=\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(\varepsilon_0-x_0^Th)^2\}\\
&=\mathbb E(\varepsilon_0^2)
-2\,\mathbb E(\varepsilon_0 x_0^Th)
+\mathbb E\{(x_0^Th)^2\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\varepsilon_0\) is independent of \(x_0\) and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_0=0\),
\[
\mathbb E(\varepsilon_0 x_0^Th)=\mathbb E\varepsilon_0\cdot \mathbb E(x_0^Th)=0.
\]
Also
\[
y_0-x_0^T\beta^*=\varepsilon_0.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*))^2\}.
}
\]

Equivalently, the excess out-of-sample prediction error is
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^Th)^2\}=h^T\Sigma h.
\]

---

## (ii) Concentration of \(\widetilde \Sigma\) in max norm

We prove that with high probability,
\[
\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}
\le B_1\lambda_0,
\qquad 
\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{\log(p/\delta)}{n}}.
\]

For fixed \(j,k\),
\[
\widetilde\Sigma_{jk}-\Sigma_{jk}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \left(x_{ij}x_{ik}-\mathbb E(x_jx_k)\right).
\]
Because \(|x_i|\le B_0\) a.s., each coordinate satisfies \(|x_{ij}|\le B_0\), so
\[
|x_{ij}x_{ik}|\le B_0^2.
\]
Thus \(x_{ij}x_{ik}\in[-B_0^2,B_0^2]\). By Hoeffding's inequality,
\[
\mathbb P\left(
\left|
\widetilde\Sigma_{jk}-\Sigma_{jk}
\right|>t
\right)
\le
2\exp\left(-\frac{nt^2}{2B_0^4}\right).
\]
Taking a union bound over all \(1\le j,k\le p\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(
\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}>t
\right)
\le
2p^2\exp\left(-\frac{nt^2}{2B_0^4}\right).
\]
Set \(t=B_1\lambda_0\). Then
\[
\mathbb P\left(
\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}>B_1\lambda_0
\right)
\le
2p^2
\exp\left(
-\frac{B_1^2}{2B_0^4}\log(p/\delta)
\right).
\]
Choose, for example,
\[
B_1=2B_0^2.
\]
Then \(B_1^2/(2B_0^4)=2\), so
\[
\mathbb P\left(
\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}>B_1\lambda_0
\right)
\le
2p^2(p/\delta)^{-2}
=
2\delta^2.
\]
For \(0<\delta\le 1\), this is at most \(2\delta\). Therefore, defining
\[
\Omega_1
:=
\left\{
\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0
\right\},
\]
we have
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(\Omega_1)\ge 1-k_1\delta
}
\]
with \(k_1=2\), for \(B_1=2B_0^2\).

---

## (iii) Compatibility/restricted eigenvalue condition for \(\widetilde\Sigma\)

Assume

\[
b^T\Sigma b\ge (\nu_0^*)^2\|b\|_2^2
\qquad\text{for all }b\in\mathbb R^p,
\]
and
\[
s\lambda_0\le \eta_0.
\]

Let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\) satisfy the cone condition
\[
\|b_{S^c}\|_1\le \xi_0\|b_S\|_1.
\]
Then
\[
\|b\|_1
=
\|b_S\|_1+\|b_{S^c}\|_1
\le
(1+\xi_0)\|b_S\|_1.
\]

On \(\Omega_1\),
\[
\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
b^T\widetilde\Sigma b
&=b^T\Sigma b+b^T(\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma)b\\
&\ge b^T\Sigma b-\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\|b\|_1^2\\
&\ge (\nu_0^*)^2\|b\|_2^2
-
B_1\lambda_0(1+\xi_0)^2\|b_S\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Also,
\[
\|b\|_2^2\ge \|b_S\|_2^2
\ge \frac{\|b_S\|_1^2}{s}.
\]
Therefore
\[
b^T\widetilde\Sigma b
\ge
\left[
\frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{s}
-
B_1\lambda_0(1+\xi_0)^2
\right]\|b_S\|_1^2.
\]
Using \(s\lambda_0\le \eta_0\),
\[
b^T\widetilde\Sigma b
\ge
\frac{
(\nu_0^*)^2-B_1\eta_0(1+\xi_0)^2
}{s}
\|b_S\|_1^2.
\]

Choose \(\eta_0>0\) small enough so that
\[
(\nu_0^*)^2-B_1\eta_0(1+\xi_0)^2>0.
\]
For example, if
\[
\eta_0\le \frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{2B_1(1+\xi_0)^2},
\]
then we may take
\[
\nu_0^2:=\frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{2}.
\]
Thus, on \(\Omega_1\),
\[
b^T\widetilde\Sigma b
\ge
\frac{\nu_0^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{
\nu_0^2\left(\sum_{j\in S}|b_j|\right)^2
\le
s\, b^T\widetilde\Sigma b.
}
\]

This is the desired compatibility condition for \(\widetilde\Sigma\).

---

## (iv) Score event \(\Omega_2\) and Lasso oracle bounds

Define the empirical noise-score vector
\[
z:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\varepsilon_i
=
\frac1nX^T\varepsilon.
\]
We will take
\[
\Omega_2
:=
\left\{
\|z\|_\infty\le A\lambda_0
\right\},
\]
for a constant \(A>0\) depending only on \(B_0\) and \(\sigma\).

### Probability bound for \(\Omega_2\)

Condition on \(X=(x_1,\dots,x_n)^T\). For each coordinate \(j\),
\[
z_j=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_{ij}\varepsilon_i.
\]
The variables \(\varepsilon_i\) are independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian, and \(|x_{ij}|\le B_0\). By the standard concentration inequality for weighted sums of independent sub-Gaussian random variables, there exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, conditionally on \(X\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(
|z_j|>t\mid X
\right)
\le
2\exp\left(
-\frac{c nt^2}{\sigma^2B_0^2}
\right).
\]
Taking a union bound over \(j=1,\dots,p\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(
\|z\|_\infty>t\mid X
\right)
\le
2p\exp\left(
-\frac{c nt^2}{\sigma^2B_0^2}
\right).
\]
Thus the same unconditional bound holds.

Now choose
\[
A:=\sigma B_0\sqrt{\frac{2}{c}}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P(\Omega_2^c)
&=
\mathbb P\left(
\|z\|_\infty>A\lambda_0
\right)\\
&\le
2p\exp\left(
-\frac{c n A^2\lambda_0^2}{\sigma^2B_0^2}
\right)\\
&=
2p\exp\left(
-2\log(p/\delta)
\right)\\
&=
2p(p/\delta)^{-2}\\
&=
\frac{2\delta^2}{p}\\
&\le 2\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(\Omega_2)\ge 1-k_2\delta
}
\]
with \(k_2=2\).

### Choice of \(\lambda\)

Let \(\xi_0>1\) be the cone constant from part (iii), and define
\[
\alpha:=\frac{\xi_0-1}{\xi_0+1}\in(0,1).
\]
Choose
\[
\boxed{
\lambda:=\frac{A}{\alpha}\lambda_0
=
A\frac{\xi_0+1}{\xi_0-1}\lambda_0.
}
\]
Then on \(\Omega_2\),
\[
\|z\|_\infty\le A\lambda_0=\alpha\lambda.
\]

### Lasso oracle inequalities

On \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), the usual Lasso basic inequality gives
\[
\frac12\|h\|_n^2+\lambda\|\beta^*+h\|_1
\le
z^Th+\lambda\|\beta^*\|_1.
\]
Using \(\|z\|_\infty\le \alpha\lambda\), one obtains the cone condition
\[
\|h_{S^c}\|_1\le \xi_0\|h_S\|_1.
\]
Then the compatibility condition from part (iii) applies:
\[
\nu_0^2\|h_S\|_1^2
\le
s\|h\|_n^2.
\]
The standard Lasso oracle inequality under compatibility therefore yields constants \(M_0<\infty\), depending only on \(B_0,\sigma,\xi_0,\nu_0\), such that on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),
\[
\boxed{
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left(x_i^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)\right)^2
=
\|h\|_n^2
\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2,
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\|\hat\beta-\beta^*\|_1
=
\|h\|_1
\le
M_0s\lambda_0.
}
\]

---

## (v) Out-of-sample error bound

By part (i),
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
h^T\Sigma h.
\]
We need to bound \(h^T\Sigma h\).

On \(\Omega_1\),
\[
\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
h^T\Sigma h
&=
h^T\widetilde\Sigma h
+
h^T(\Sigma-\widetilde\Sigma)h\\
&\le
h^T\widetilde\Sigma h
+
\|\Sigma-\widetilde\Sigma\|_{\max}\|h\|_1^2\\
&\le
\|h\|_n^2
+
B_1\lambda_0\|h\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
On \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), by part (iv),
\[
\|h\|_n^2\le M_0s\lambda_0^2,
\qquad
\|h\|_1\le M_0s\lambda_0.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
h^T\Sigma h
&\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1\lambda_0(M_0s\lambda_0)^2\\
&=
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1M_0^2s^2\lambda_0^3\\
&=
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2s\lambda_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Using assumption (A4), \(s\lambda_0\le \eta_0\), we obtain
\[
h^T\Sigma h
\le
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\]
Let
\[
M_1:=M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0.
\]
Then on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),
\[
h^T\Sigma h\le M_1s\lambda_0^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
\le
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
M_1|S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2.
}
\]

Moreover,
\[
\mathbb P(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)
\ge
1-(k_1+k_2)\delta,
\]
with \(k_1,k_2\) absolute constants.

z_j=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_{ij}\varepsilon_i.
\]
The variables \(\varepsilon_i\) are independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian, and \(|x_{ij}|\le B_0\). By the standard concentration inequality for weighted sums of independent sub-Gaussian random variables, there exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, conditionally on \(X\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(
|z_j|>t\mid X
\right)
\le
2\exp\left(
-\frac{c nt^2}{\sigma^2B_0^2}
\right).
\]
Taking a union bound over \(j=1,\dots,p\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(
\|z\|_\infty>t\mid X
\right)
\le
2p\exp\left(
-\frac{c nt^2}{\sigma^2B_0^2}
\right).
\]
Thus the same unconditional bound holds.

Now choose
\[
A:=\sigma B_0\sqrt{\frac{2}{c}}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P(\Omega_2^c)
&=
\mathbb P\left(
\|z\|_\infty>A\lambda_0
\right)\\
&\le
2p\exp\left(
-\frac{c n A^2\lambda_0^2}{\sigma^2B_0^2}
\right)\\
&=
2p\exp\left(
-2\log(p/\delta)
\right)\\
&=
2p(p/\delta)^{-2}\\
&=
\frac{2\delta^2}{p}\\
&\le 2\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(\Omega_2)\ge 1-k_2\delta
}
\]
with \(k_2=2\).

### Choice of \(\lambda\)

Let \(\xi_0>1\) be the cone constant from part (iii), and define
\[
\alpha:=\frac{\xi_0-1}{\xi_0+1}\in(0,1).
\]
Choose
\[
\boxed{
\lambda:=\frac{A}{\alpha}\lambda_0
=
A\frac{\xi_0+1}{\xi_0-1}\lambda_0.
}
\]
Then on \(\Omega_2\),
\[
\|z\|_\infty\le A\lambda_0=\alpha\lambda.
\]

### Lasso oracle inequalities

On \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), the usual Lasso basic inequality gives
\[
\frac12\|h\|_n^2+\lambda\|\beta^*+h\|_1
\le
z^Th+\lambda\|\beta^*\|_1.
\]
Using \(\|z\|_\infty\le \alpha\lambda\), one obtains the cone condition
\[
\|h_{S^c}\|_1\le \xi_0\|h_S\|_1.
\]
Then the compatibility condition from part (iii) applies:
\[
\nu_0^2\|h_S\|_1^2
\le
s\|h\|_n^2.
\]
The standard Lasso oracle inequality under compatibility therefore yields constants \(M_0<\infty\), depending only on \(B_0,\sigma,\xi_0,\nu_0\), such that on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),
\[
\boxed{
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left(x_i^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)\right)^2
=
\|h\|_n^2
\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2,
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\|\hat\beta-\beta^*\|_1
=
\|h\|_1
\le
M_0s\lambda_0.
}
\]

---

## (v) Out-of-sample error bound

By part (i),
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
h^T\Sigma h.
\]
We need to bound \(h^T\Sigma h\).

On \(\Omega_1\),
\[
\|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
h^T\Sigma h
&=
h^T\widetilde\Sigma h
+
h^T(\Sigma-\widetilde\Sigma)h\\
&\le
h^T\widetilde\Sigma h
+
\|\Sigma-\widetilde\Sigma\|_{\max}\|h\|_1^2\\
&\le
\|h\|_n^2
+
B_1\lambda_0\|h\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
On \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), by part (iv),
\[
\|h\|_n^2\le M_0s\lambda_0^2,
\qquad
\|h\|_1\le M_0s\lambda_0.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
h^T\Sigma h
&\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1\lambda_0(M_0s\lambda_0)^2\\
&=
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1M_0^2s^2\lambda_0^3\\
&=
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2s\lambda_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Using assumption (A4), \(s\lambda_0\le \eta_0\), we obtain
\[
h^T\Sigma h
\le
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\]
Let
\[
M_1:=M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0.
\]
Then on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),
\[
h^T\Sigma h\le M_1s\lambda_0^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
\le
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
M_1|S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2.
}
\]

Moreover,
\[
\mathbb P(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)
\ge
1-(k_1+k_2)\delta,
\]
with \(k_1,k_2\) absolute constants.
